about.titleHighlight: BMW Z4 M Roadster M Coupe ENGINE
paragraphs: The Z4 M was produced from 2006 to 2008 as a standalone M-badged variant of the E85/E86-generation Z4 — available as both a Roadster and a fixed-roof M Coupe. Under the bonnet sits the S54 — a 3.2-litre naturally-aspirated inline-six, the same engine used in the E46 M3 of the same era. The S54 was produced in two distinct power outputs during the E46 M3's run — the Z4 M received the later 343hp version of the engine. The Z4 M is no longer in production, but we continue to rebuild and replace engines for every one still on the road.
about.boldParagraph: The Z4 M Roadster M Coupe is no longer in production, but we continue to rebuild and replace engines for every one still on the road.

compatibility.titlePre: BMW Z4 M Roadster M Coupe ENGINE
compatibility.intro: The Z4 M uses a single engine across its entire production run — the S54. However, because the S54 was also used in the E46 M3 in two different power outputs (338hp in early cars, 343hp in later cars), and because some Z4 M variants were sold in different markets with minor specification differences, we always confirm your exact ECU and engine specification by registration before any work begins. This matters because compatibility for replacement parts or engine management work can differ between early and late S54 cars.
